answer: With a Verified email inbox bound by attestation certificate with a ninety-day rotation cooldown, the account is only as strong as its binding: the verified email inbox answers a fresh challenge, the attestation certificate is recorded, and a ninety-day rotation cooldown keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so losing the channel means losing the identity, and fakes cannot hide behind throwaway channels. One knoll proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of bindings. The thread and the harbor agree: no channel, no trust.
